title: quest browser outlives its workspace indefinitely: three daemons alive, one for 44 hours, all with deleted working directories
description:
Reported by opum-cli-e2e 2026-09-18 and CONFIRMED HERE by direct process inspection rather than from their report. A quest browser daemon keeps running after the workspace it was started against has been deleted, with no upper bound observed.

Measured on this host at 2026-09-19T00:30Z, all three orphaned to init (ppid 1):

  pid    started                    elapsed       binary
  51327  Fri Sep 18 19:07:21 2026   22m           global install
  92526  Thu Sep 17 15:02:16 2026   1d 04:27      global install
  95162  Wed Sep 16 22:38:57 2026   1d 20:50      candidate install under .opum-candidates/0.7.1-pair

Every cwd is a deleted temp workspace of the form /private/var/folders/.../opum-e2e-ws-*/quest-project-*. lsof on a live .quest shows they hold no workspace open; they are simply alive.

TWO FACTS THAT NARROW IT, both measured rather than inferred:

1. The instances span TWO DIFFERENT INSTALLS -- one global, one a candidate install under .opum-candidates -- so nothing about how a candidate is bound explains it.

2. All three were spawned by opum-cli-e2e harness runs, including pid 51327 from their control matrix tonight. That explains the INSTANCES, not the BEHAVIOUR. A browser that outlives its workspace by 44 hours is a quest defect regardless of who started it; the harness spawning them is why there are three rather than why they survive. opum-cli-e2e made this split themselves and filed the reaping half as their TASK-91, which stays theirs.

An earlier suspicion that this repository own test suite leaks one was checked and is WRONG: every cwd is an opum-e2e-ws path, and this repository tests run bun src/cli/main.ts rather than an installed binary. Recorded because it was the obvious first guess.

NOT investigated yet: whether browser --port 0 --json installs any parent-death or workspace-death watch at all, whether the daemon should exit when its root disappears, and whether it should exit when its parent does. The daemons were deliberately left running for inspection -- opum-cli-e2e offered to kill them and was asked to hold.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The conditions under which quest browser should terminate are decided and written down -- at minimum whether it exits when the workspace root it was started against no longer exists.

A browser started against a workspace that is then deleted terminates rather than running indefinitely, proven by a test that creates a workspace, starts the daemon, removes the workspace and observes the exit.

Every leaked daemon alive on this host at fix time is reaped -- enumerated at that moment rather than against the count in this record, which was three when filed and four an hour later. The decision about parent-death behaviour is recorded even if the answer is that no parent watch is wanted.

implementationNotes:
EVIDENCE CORRECTED AND STRENGTHENED by opum-cli-e2e, 2026-09-19. The description above says three daemons; there are FOUR, and the leak rate is now measured rather than inferred.

WHAT CHANGED. I filed this with three daemons and declined to carry a per-run frequency claim, because my process list could not support one -- the cwds are deleted, so nothing on my side tied a daemon to a particular run. I suggested matching the workspace token against their run log as the way to turn the inference into evidence. Their harness does record the workspace, so the match was available:

  pid 44029  19:35:00   opum-e2e-ws-TtCncZ -> runs/prepublish-quest0.9.0-lore0.8.0
  pid 51327  19:07:21   opum-e2e-ws-fiYBLC -> runs/control-darwin-arm64-quest0.7.1-lore0.7.0
  pid 92526  Thu 15:02  opum-e2e-ws-fvZFgk -> NONE FOUND (run directory not retained)
  pid 95162  Wed 22:38  opum-e2e-ws-AsWOco -> runs/2026-09-17T03-38-20-663Z

FOUR daemons, FOUR distinct workspaces, no workspace appearing twice. That is one per matrix run established BY NAME rather than by arithmetic, which is a different and better claim than the one either of us started with.

TWO CORRECTIONS RECORDED AS CORRECTIONS RATHER THAN SILENTLY APPLIED:

1. Their attribution of pid 51327 was backwards. They believed it came from the pre-publish qualification run; it is from the CONTROL run. The pre-publish daemon is pid 44029, which did not exist when I measured.

2. My count of three was accurate WHEN TAKEN and is stale rather than wrong. The fourth daemon started at 19:35, after my observation; they ran exactly one matrix in the interval, so the count moving from three to four is itself corroboration of the one-per-run rate rather than a discrepancy needing explanation. A dated measurement going stale is the normal way a dated measurement ends.

A SECOND, SMALLER FINDING WORTH ITS OWN FIX. One daemon (fvZFgk) matched nothing, because runs/ is gitignored and older run directories get cleaned. So ATTRIBUTION HAS A SHELF LIFE: a leaked process whose only identifier is a deleted cwd AND a discarded run directory cannot be attributed at all. The fix for the leak and the fix for the attribution window are different fixes, and the second one is invisible until someone tries to attribute an old process and cannot.

SCOPE UNCHANGED. The daemon behaviour is still this repository defect and the reaping half is still theirs (their TASK-91). Four daemons are deliberately left running for inspection; they will not reap without asking.
